Quick triage notes — attaching perf-sample.log with representative trace.

What we see:
- The customer’s route was switched to qprofile v2.1 at ~08:40 PDT during a staged rollout. v2.1 changed packing alignment for the quantized kernels (improves avg token cost) but introduced a heavier decode path for short sequences in this model family.
- For low-seqlen hotpath traffic (what HarborLine uses on checkout), the new decode path increases per-token scheduling jitter and causes degraded batching efficiency on specific instance types. That explains p95 and throughput drop + sporadic decode failures when the runtime backpressure triggers request aborts (observed 502s).

Mitigation options (ordered):
1) Immediate rollback to qprofile v1.8 for HarborLine’s variant (fastest, restores baseline p95 and throughput, minor cost increase).
2) Pin HarborLine traffic to the v1.8 variant and continue controlled rollout of v2.x to other customers.
3) Apply a micro-patch to the runtime decode scheduler (longer, needs infra window).

I recommend option 1 + short post-rollback validation window. I can execute rollback if we get authorization from CS/TS and account. We should plan a postmortem and add a canary that includes short-seq checkout traffic next time.

Attachments: perf-sample.log

—Vivek

Subject: Re: Urgent: Production latency spike after model update — rollback complete

Rollback to qprofile v1.8 for HarborLine completed at 12:50 PDT (applied only to the HarborLine routing policy). Post-rollback quick checks:
- p95 back to baseline: median across sampled nodes 290ms (pre-incident baseline ~280–300ms).
- Throughput restored to within 97% of pre-rollout levels.
- Token decode error rate collapsed to background levels (seen in earlier logs).

Notes and next steps:
- We observed a small average-quality delta for a tiny subset of longer-reply prompts (v2.1 did a modest improvement there). We will quantify quality delta in the postmortem and propose a targeted canary (include HarborLine short-seq traffic in next rollout) before reattempting v2.x.
- Please see postrollback_p95_summary_20260925.csv and the JIRA INF-9821 for the follow-up ticket to track the runtime micro-patch.

I’ll remain on standby for 2 hours in case you see any regressions.

—Vivek
